title: Blinkist – The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People

items.meaning: 角落辦公室（象徵高階職位、事業成功）
items.usage: 名詞片語；大樓角落、有兩面窗的辦公室通常給高層主管，所以常用來比喻「升到高位」。常見：land / get a corner office。
items.example: She worked her way up from intern to a corner office in just ten years.
items.trans: 她只花十年就從實習生一路升到高階主管。

items.usage: a sense of + 抽象名詞是高頻搭配：a sense of achievement / purpose / belonging。形容詞常用 deep、real、great。動詞搭配：give sb / feel a sense of accomplishment。
items.example: Finishing the marathon gave me a real sense of accomplishment.
items.trans: 跑完馬拉松讓我很有成就感。

items.usage: 不及物動詞，後接 to + 名詞或原形動詞；比 want 正式，帶「有抱負」的語氣。文中 goals to which we aspire ＝ goals we aspire to（見 #18）。名詞 aspiration、形容詞 aspiring（aspiring writer 有志成為作家的人）。
items.example: Many junior engineers aspire to lead their own teams one day.
items.trans: 許多資淺工程師都渴望有朝一日能帶領自己的團隊。

items.meaning: 目標超出自己能力所及；心有餘而力不足
items.usage: 改寫自諺語 a man's reach should exceed his grasp（人的志向應超越能力所及，Robert Browning 詩句）。grasp 在此是「能掌握的範圍」。原諺語是正面鼓勵，文中則表示挫折感。
items.example: Early in my career, I often felt my ambitions exceeded my grasp.
items.trans: 職涯初期，我常覺得自己的抱負超出能力所及。

items.usage: tap into ＝ 開發、利用（原意是在桶上開孔取用）。常見受詞：potential、talent、a market、resources、emotions。近義 unlock / unleash one's potential。
items.example: Good managers know how to tap into their team's hidden potential.
items.trans: 好的主管懂得發掘團隊潛藏的潛力。

items.usage: 放句首或句中，引出出乎意料或回答前文疑問的事實。文中接在 If only there were a way…! 之後，回答「還真的有」。近義 as it happens。
items.example: I thought the meeting was cancelled, but as it turns out, it was just moved to Friday.
items.trans: 我以為會議取消了，結果只是改到星期五。

items.meaning: 充分利用、發揮最大價值
items.usage: get the most out of + 人／物／經驗。也可說 make the most of（make the most of 多接機會、時間）。用於自己時：get the most out of yourself ＝ 發揮自己最大的能力。
items.example: To get the most out of this course, do the exercises after each lesson.
items.trans: 想從這門課獲得最大收穫，每堂課後都要做練習。

items.usage: 常見於簡報、教學：take you through the details / the process。近義 walk sb through（更口語）。
items.example: Let me take you through the key figures from last quarter.
items.trans: 讓我帶大家看一下上一季的關鍵數據。

items.usage: 接在最高級後：the best / most influential … of all time。GOAT ＝ greatest of all time。
items.example: Many critics call it one of the greatest films of all time.
items.trans: 許多影評人稱它為有史以來最偉大的電影之一。

items.term: be on top of the best-seller lists
items.usage: 也可說 top the best-seller lists（top 當動詞）。注意 be on top of sth 另有「掌控、跟上進度」之意（stay on top of my emails），需靠上下文判斷。
items.example: Her debut novel has been on top of the best-seller lists for months.
items.trans: 她的處女作已經在暢銷榜上名列前茅好幾個月了。

items.usage: take charge of + 事物／局面／人生。強調主動接手、掌控；比較 be in charge of 是「負責（的狀態）」。與 #15 cultivate 同屬本書核心：主動經營自己的生活。
items.example: After the manager left, Lisa took charge of the project.
items.trans: 經理離職後，Lisa 接手負責這個專案。

items.usage: 常見：highly / deeply influential、an influential figure / book / thinker。動詞、名詞為 influence。重音在 -en-。
items.example: He is one of the most influential voices in the tech industry.
items.trans: 他是科技業最有影響力的聲音之一。

items.meaning: 有洞察力的、見解深刻的
items.usage: 形容意見、分析、評論或人：insightful advice / comments / analysis。名詞 insight（gain insight into…）。常用於稱讚會議發言：That's very insightful.
items.example: Thanks for your insightful feedback on the proposal.
items.trans: 謝謝你對提案提出深具見解的意見。

items.meaning: 有啟發性的、有教育意義的
items.usage: 多形容例子、經驗、比較：an instructive example / experience。易混淆 instructional（教學用的，如 instructional video），instructive 強調「讓人學到東西」。
items.example: It's instructive to compare how the two companies handled the crisis.
items.trans: 比較這兩家公司如何處理危機，很有啟發性。

items.meaning: 培養、養成（習慣、關係、形象）
items.usage: 原意「耕種」，引申為長期用心經營：cultivate a habit / a lifestyle / relationships / an image。比 develop 更有「慢慢培養」的感覺。與 #11 搭配使用。
items.example: She has cultivated strong relationships with key clients over the years.
items.trans: 多年來她和重要客戶培養出深厚的關係。

items.usage: 最常見 a self-help book / guide / guru。書店分類常寫 Self-Help。有時帶輕微貶意，暗指內容空泛。
items.example: I used to be skeptical of self-help books, but this one changed my mind.
items.trans: 我以前對自我成長書很存疑，但這本改變了我的看法。

items.term: If only there were a way to…!
items.usage: If only + 假設語氣（過去式，be 動詞用 were）表達強烈願望。文章常先用這句製造渴望，再用 Well, as it turns out, there is.（#6）揭曉答案，是很好用的開場手法。
items.example: If only there were a way to finish all these reports before Friday!
items.trans: 要是有辦法在星期五前把這些報告全做完就好了！

items.term: N + to which + S + V（goals to which we aspire）
items.meaning: 介係詞移到關係代名詞前的正式寫法
items.usage: goals to which we aspire ＝ goals (that) we aspire to。介係詞前移讓語氣更正式，適合書面、簡報；口語通常把介係詞留在句尾。類似：the project on which I worked / the people with whom we partner。
items.example: These are the standards to which every team member should be held.
items.trans: 這些是每位團隊成員都應遵守的標準。

items.term: To get the most out of X, you just need to…
items.usage: 不定詞片語放句首表目的，再用 just need to 把方法說得簡單易行，常見於建議、教學、行銷文案。可換成 To succeed in…, you just need to…
items.example: To get the most out of your new phone, you just need to update a few settings.
items.trans: 想讓新手機發揮最大效能，你只需要調整幾項設定。

items.term: …, and there is a very good reason for this.
items.usage: 先陳述現象，再用這句預告接下來要解釋原因，引起讀者好奇。簡報中也好用：Sales doubled last quarter, and there's a very good reason for this.
items.example: Our customer retention is the highest in the industry, and there is a very good reason for this.
items.trans: 我們的顧客留存率是業界最高，而這背後有很充分的理由。

items.usage: find one's way around + 地方＝熟悉環境、會認路；find one's way to＝找到去某處的路。也可比喻摸清新工作、新系統。
items.example: It took me a week to find my way around the new office.
items.trans: 我花了一週才摸熟新辦公室的環境。

items.usage: 反義 in the long term / in the long run。也可當形容詞 short-term（short-term goals）。常用來對比短期與長期效果。
items.example: Cutting prices may boost sales in the short term, but it hurts our brand.
items.trans: 降價短期內也許能提升銷售，但會傷害品牌。

items.usage: 表示非預期或不理想的結果：end up lost / end up working late / end up in hospital。
items.example: We missed the last train and ended up taking a taxi home.
items.trans: 我們錯過末班車，最後只好搭計程車回家。

items.usage: grasp 當動詞＝透徹理解，比 understand 更有「抓住要點」的感覺：grasp the concept / the importance of。名詞用法見 #4。
items.example: Once you grasp the basic principles, the rest is easy.
items.trans: 一旦掌握基本原則，其他就簡單了。

items.usage: make a habit of + V-ing；否定常說 I don't make a habit of it（我不常這樣）。近義 get into the habit of。
items.example: I've made a habit of reviewing my notes every morning.
items.trans: 我養成每天早上複習筆記的習慣。

items.usage: 回顧過去的時間、經歷；look back on 多帶感情或反思。In looking back, …＝回頭看。
items.example: Looking back on my first job, I learned a lot from my mistakes.
items.trans: 回顧第一份工作，我從錯誤中學到很多。

items.meaning: 帶來（根本的）改變、有重大影響
items.usage: make a difference＝有影響、有差別；可加 big / real / huge / fundamental。make a difference to sth＝對某事有影響。與 #37 superficial 對比。
items.example: A short daily walk can make a real difference to your health.
items.trans: 每天短暫散步對健康有很大的幫助。

items.meaning: 使 A 與 B 一致、對齊
items.usage: 職場超常用：align our goals with the company strategy；be aligned with＝與……一致。名詞 alignment（in alignment with）。
items.example: We need to align our marketing plan with the sales targets.
items.trans: 我們需要讓行銷計畫與業績目標一致。

items.usage: lasting＝持久的：a lasting impression / impact / peace。近義 long-lasting、enduring；反義 short-lived、temporary。
items.example: Crash diets rarely achieve lasting results.
items.trans: 速成節食很少能帶來持久的效果。

items.usage: 與 in theory 對比：In theory it works, but in practice…。put sth into practice＝付諸實行。
items.example: The policy sounds simple, but in practice it's hard to enforce.
items.trans: 這項政策聽起來簡單，但實際上很難執行。

items.usage: work on sth＝努力改進某事（work on my English / my presentation skills）。work on yourself 強調從內在改變，呼應本段的 Character Ethic。
items.example: Before blaming others, try working on yourself first.
items.trans: 在責怪別人之前，先試著改善自己。

items.usage: 常獨立成句：That's easier said than done. 或放句中：Of course, this is easier said than done.
items.example: Just stop worrying? That's easier said than done.
items.trans: 別擔心就好？說得容易做起來難。

items.usage: 用來總結前文；近義 in a word、to sum up、in a nutshell（口語）。
items.example: In short, we need more time and a bigger budget.
items.trans: 簡單說，我們需要更多時間和更多預算。

items.usage: 強調不貪多、按部就班。相關 one step at a time（一步一步來）、one by one。
items.example: Let's tackle these problems one at a time.
items.trans: 我們一個一個處理這些問題吧。

items.usage: 正式用語，指看待事物的基本模式；a paradigm shift＝典範轉移、根本性的觀念改變（商業文章常見）。g 不發音。
items.example: Remote work has caused a paradigm shift in how companies hire.
items.trans: 遠距工作讓企業招聘方式出現根本性的轉變。

items.usage: 單數 ethic 指一套價值觀，常見 work ethic（職業道德、敬業精神）；複數 ethics＝倫理學、道德規範。形容詞 ethical。
items.example: She's known for her strong work ethic.
items.trans: 她以敬業精神著稱。

items.usage: 形容改變、傷口、了解、人：superficial changes / knowledge / wounds。反義 fundamental（#27）、deep、profound。
items.example: The redesign was purely superficial; the app still crashes.
items.trans: 這次改版純粹是表面功夫，App 還是會當機。

items.usage: 只放名詞前：underlying cause / problem / principle / assumption。常用於分析問題根源。
items.example: We need to address the underlying cause, not just the symptoms.
items.trans: 我們要處理根本原因，而不只是表面症狀。

items.usage: have / show / feel empathy for sb；形容詞 empathetic / empathic。易混淆 sympathy（同情）：empathy 是能設身處地感受。
items.example: Good leaders show empathy for their team members.
items.trans: 好的領導者對團隊成員展現同理心。

items.usage: perceive A as B＝把 A 視為 B；be perceived as＝被認為是。名詞 perception（public perception 大眾觀感）。比 see 正式。
items.example: Customers perceive our brand as reliable but expensive.
items.trans: 顧客認為我們的品牌可靠但昂貴。

items.usage: 用情境＋提問開場，讓讀者代入，再引出主題。簡報、文章開頭很好用；後面常接 Well, … 給答案（同 #6、#17 的手法）。
items.example: Imagine you're starting a new job tomorrow. How will you make a good first impression?
items.trans: 想像你明天要開始新工作，你會怎麼留下好的第一印象？

items.term: While X can be useful, it's far more valuable to…
items.meaning: 雖然 X 有用，但……更有價值
items.usage: While 表讓步，先承認一方再強調另一方；far 加強比較級。適合提建議、做比較。
items.example: While online courses can be useful, it's far more valuable to practice with real clients.
items.trans: 雖然線上課程有幫助，但和真實客戶實際練習更有價值。

items.term: become the kind of person who…
items.usage: 把目標從「做某事」轉為「成為某種人」，是本書核心觀念（呼應 #31）。the kind of + N + who / that…
items.example: If you want to be trusted, become the kind of person who keeps promises.
items.trans: 想被信任，就成為那種說到做到的人。

items.term: X requires that + S + (should) V原形
items.usage: require、suggest、insist、recommend 後接 that 子句時，動詞用原形（假設語氣）：requires that you cultivate（不是 cultivates）。正式書面常見。
items.example: The new policy requires that every employee complete the training by May.
items.trans: 新政策要求每位員工在五月前完成訓練。

items.usage: millennia 是 millennium（千年）的複數。類似 for centuries / for decades（第 1 段用過 for decades）。誇飾用法：for ages。
items.example: Humans have told stories around the fire for millennia.
items.trans: 人類圍著火堆說故事已有數千年。

items.usage: point to＝把某事當作原因或證據提出：Experts point to rising costs as the main reason. 比 blame 中性。
items.example: Analysts point to weak demand as the cause of the drop.
items.trans: 分析師認為需求疲弱是下滑的原因。

items.usage: reign 原指君王統治，g 不發音（同 rain）。reign supreme＝在某領域最重要、最強。
items.example: In this company, the customer reigns supreme.
items.trans: 在這家公司，顧客至上。

items.usage: 後接無法控制的力量：at the mercy of the weather / the market / the boss。與 #64 proactive 的精神相反。
items.example: Small farmers are at the mercy of the weather.
items.trans: 小農只能看天吃飯。

items.term: the crucial difference between A and B
items.meaning: A 與 B 的關鍵差異
items.usage: crucial＝極重要、關鍵的，比 important 強：a crucial role / decision / moment。
items.example: The crucial difference between the two plans is cost.
items.trans: 這兩個方案的關鍵差異在於成本。

items.usage: capacity for + 抽象名詞＝天生或潛在能力：capacity for self-awareness / learning / growth。另義「容量、產能」（production capacity）。
items.example: Children have an amazing capacity for learning languages.
items.trans: 孩子學語言的能力驚人。

items.usage: 正式。原義「欠某人人情、受恩於」，引申為「受……支配、不得不聽從」：beholden to shareholders / special interests。
items.example: Independent media should not be beholden to advertisers.
items.trans: 獨立媒體不應受廣告商左右。

items.usage: 近義 take control of one's fate / life；呼應 #11 take charge of。destiny 偏正面、宏大，fate 常帶無奈。
items.example: Education gives people the chance to determine their own destiny.
items.trans: 教育讓人有機會掌握自己的命運。

items.usage: positive 當名詞（複數）＝優點、好處；反義 the negatives。近義 look on the bright side。
items.example: Even after the setback, she chose to focus on the positives.
items.trans: 即使遭遇挫折，她仍選擇看好的一面。

items.usage: direct 當動詞＝引導、導向；也可說 channel one's energy into。可與本段末的 focus your energy on 互換。
items.example: Instead of complaining, direct your energy toward finding a solution.
items.trans: 與其抱怨，不如把精力用在找解決方法上。

items.usage: in command of one's emotions / the situation＝掌控得住；比 in control of 更有「指揮」的語感。
items.example: She stayed calm and in command of the meeting.
items.trans: 她保持冷靜，完全掌控會議。

items.meaning: 撐過去、度過難關（病痛、危機）
items.usage: 不及物：He pulled through. 也可 pull sb through（幫某人度過）。近義 get through、survive。
items.example: The company pulled through the recession thanks to loyal customers.
items.trans: 靠著忠實顧客，公司撐過了經濟衰退。

items.usage: take care to + 原形動詞＝刻意謹慎地做；比 be careful to 正式。
items.example: Take extra care to check the figures before sending the report.
items.trans: 寄出報告前要特別留意核對數字。

items.usage: 正式：the best course of action / decide on a course of action。常用於決策討論。
items.example: After reviewing the data, we agreed on a course of action.
items.trans: 檢視資料後，我們達成行動方案的共識。

items.usage: b 不發音。succumb to temptation / pressure / an illness。比 give in to 正式。
items.example: Don't succumb to pressure to cut corners.
items.trans: 別因壓力就屈服而便宜行事。

items.usage: 比喻暫時抽離以看清全局：step back and look at the big picture。另義「卸下職務」（step back from the role）。
items.example: Sometimes you need to step back to see what's really going on.
items.trans: 有時你得退一步才看得清真正的狀況。

items.usage: root cause analysis＝根本原因分析（職場常用）。近義 underlying cause（#38）。
items.example: We fixed the bug, but we still don't know the root cause.
items.trans: 我們修好了錯誤，但仍不知道根本原因。

items.usage: 正式或文學性；vexed question＝爭論不休的難題。形容詞 vexing。
items.example: The problem has vexed engineers for years.
items.trans: 這個問題困擾工程師多年。

items.meaning: 決定論的（認為一切由外因決定）
items.usage: 名詞 determinism。文中解釋為「命運由外在影響決定」。動詞 determine（#52）。
items.example: His view of human behavior is too deterministic.
items.trans: 他對人類行為的看法太偏決定論。

items.meaning: 主動積極的、先發制人的
items.usage: 本書第一個習慣。反義 reactive（被動回應的）。職場常用：take a proactive approach。
items.example: Be proactive and raise issues before they become problems.
items.trans: 要主動，在問題擴大前就提出來。

items.meaning: 沉思鬱悶、悶悶不樂地想
items.usage: brood about / over sth＝一直想著不愉快的事。名詞 brood 另義「一窩雛鳥」。
items.example: There's no point brooding over the mistake.
items.trans: 一直為那個錯誤悶悶不樂沒有意義。

items.usage: dire circumstances / consequences / straits；be in dire need of＝急需。
items.example: The hospital is in dire need of more nurses.
items.trans: 這家醫院急需更多護理師。

items.usage: 動詞 torment /tɔːrˈment/（折磨）；名詞 torment /ˈtɔːr.ment/（痛苦），注意重音不同。
items.example: He eventually forgave his former tormentors.
items.trans: 他最後原諒了曾經折磨他的人。

items.usage: foster creativity / collaboration / a culture of…；近義 cultivate（#15）、nurture。另義「寄養」（foster parents）。
items.example: We want to foster a culture of open feedback.
items.trans: 我們希望培養開放回饋的文化。

items.usage: 可數或不可數：face / endure hardship、financial hardship。比 difficulty 更沉重。
items.example: Many families faced financial hardship during the pandemic.
items.trans: 疫情期間許多家庭陷入經濟困境。

items.meaning: 是什麼讓 X 成為 X？
items.usage: make + 受詞 + 名詞補語，用同一個字製造巧妙效果：What makes you you? / What makes a leader a leader? 適合開場提問。
items.example: What makes a great team a great team?
items.trans: 是什麼讓一支優秀團隊之所以優秀？

items.term: Some argue that…. Others point to…. Still others insist that…
items.meaning: 有人主張……；有人歸因於……；還有人堅持……
items.usage: 列舉三種觀點的經典句型，Still others 是第三組。之後常接 The truth is…（#72）提出作者立場。
items.example: Some argue that AI will create jobs. Others point to the risk of layoffs. Still others insist it's too early to tell.
items.trans: 有人認為 AI 會創造工作，有人指出裁員風險，還有人堅持現在下定論還太早。

items.term: The truth is, none of these … is sufficient.
items.usage: The truth is, + 句子 用來推翻前面的觀點、提出真相。none of + 複數名詞，正式寫作常配單數動詞。
items.example: The truth is, none of these solutions is perfect.
items.trans: 事實上，這些方案都不完美。

items.term: Rather than + V原形, S + V…
items.usage: Rather than 放句首時接原形動詞（Rather than lose hope / brood）。近義 Instead of + V-ing。
items.example: Rather than wait for instructions, she started drafting the plan herself.
items.trans: 她沒有等指示，而是自己開始擬計畫。

items.usage: 承上啟下的轉場句，簡報超好用：…, which brings us to our next point.
items.example: Costs keep rising, which brings us to the question of pricing.
items.trans: 成本持續上升，這就帶出了定價的問題。

items.usage: die 的委婉說法，較禮貌；相關 passing（n.）：after his passing。
items.example: Her grandfather passed away peacefully last year.
items.trans: 她的祖父去年安詳離世。

items.usage: take turns + V-ing 或 take turns to V；in turn＝依序。
items.example: We take turns leading the weekly meeting.
items.trans: 我們輪流主持每週會議。

items.usage: deliver 搭配演說類：deliver a speech / a presentation / a keynote。eulogy 開頭唸 /juː/。
items.example: His best friend delivered a moving eulogy at the funeral.
items.trans: 他最好的朋友在葬禮上致了感人的悼詞。

items.usage: 原指融化，比喻擔憂、壓力、阻力慢慢消失：My worries melted away.
items.example: As soon as she started speaking, her nerves melted away.
items.trans: 她一開口，緊張感就消散了。

items.usage: 反義 go out of focus。也可 bring sth into focus（使……清楚）。
items.example: After the meeting, our priorities finally came into focus.
items.trans: 開完會後，我們的優先事項終於清楚了。

items.usage: 文中指「留給後世」：leave a legacy behind。也指把人或物落下：leave my phone behind。
items.example: What kind of legacy do you want to leave behind?
items.trans: 你想留下什麼樣的影響？

items.meaning: 把事情想清楚、通盤考量
items.usage: think sth through＝徹底想過各種後果，再做決定；與 #105 呼應。
items.example: Don't rush. Take a day to think things through.
items.trans: 別急，花一天把事情想清楚。

items.usage: carry out a plan / a survey / an order / research；比 do 正式。
items.example: The team carried out the plan exactly as designed.
items.trans: 團隊完全照設計執行了計畫。

items.usage: 原指變魔術變出來；conjure up a plan＝構思出計畫；conjure up images of…＝讓人聯想到。
items.example: The smell of coffee conjures up memories of my college days.
items.trans: 咖啡香讓我想起大學時光。

items.usage: 承接前面兩個選項：不論是 A 或 B，結論都一樣。口語常用 Either way, it's fine with me.
items.example: We can meet on Monday or Tuesday. Either way, I'll send the agenda tonight.
items.trans: 我們週一或週二見都行，不管哪天我今晚都會寄議程。

items.usage: put up a building / a tent / a sign / a poster。另義 put up with＝忍受（易混淆）。
items.example: They put up a new office building in just eight months.
items.trans: 他們只花八個月就蓋好新辦公大樓。

items.usage: draft＝草擬（draft a proposal / an email）；blueprint 比喻詳細計畫：a blueprint for success。
items.example: Before expanding overseas, we drafted a clear blueprint.
items.trans: 在拓展海外前，我們先擬好清楚的藍圖。

items.usage: chaotic 開頭唸 /keɪ/（名詞 chaos /ˈkeɪ.ɑːs/）。口語也說 a total mess。
items.example: Without a schedule, the event would have been a chaotic disaster.
items.trans: 如果沒有時程表，活動會亂成一團。

items.usage: costly＝昂貴的、代價大的（不是副詞）：a costly error / delay。make a mistake 不說 do a mistake。
items.example: Rushing the launch led us to make costly mistakes.
items.trans: 倉促上市讓我們犯下代價高昂的錯誤。

items.usage: sphere＝領域、範圍：public / private sphere、sphere of influence（勢力範圍）。
items.example: In the professional sphere, reliability matters more than talent.
items.trans: 在職場上，可靠比才華更重要。

items.usage: flesh out a plan / an idea / a draft＝把骨架加上血肉，讓內容更完整。
items.example: Can you flesh out these bullet points before the meeting?
items.trans: 會議前你可以把這些重點補充得更完整嗎？

items.usage: 近義 in advance、beforehand。ahead of schedule＝比預定進度提前。
items.example: Please submit your questions ahead of time.
items.trans: 請事先提交你的問題。

items.usage: mission statement 原指企業宗旨聲明；本書延伸為寫下個人價值與人生目標。
items.example: Our company's mission statement is printed on every badge.
items.trans: 公司的使命宣言印在每張識別證上。

items.usage: uphold＝維護、支持：uphold a principle / the law / standards。過去式 upheld。
items.example: Leaders must uphold the values they ask others to follow.
items.trans: 領導者必須堅守自己要求別人遵守的價值觀。

items.usage: stay on track 近義（職場更常用）；反義 go off track / lose one's way。呼應 #21 find one's way。
items.example: Regular check-ins help the team stay on the right path.
items.trans: 定期確認進度能幫助團隊保持在正軌上。

items.meaning: 病態的、（過度關注）死亡陰暗面的
items.usage: morbid curiosity / humor / thoughts；口語 That's a bit morbid.＝有點陰森。
items.example: Sorry for the morbid question, but do you have a will?
items.trans: 抱歉問個有點觸霉頭的問題，你有立遺囑嗎？

items.usage: step to / take the podium＝上台發言。lectern 是講桌。
items.example: The CEO stepped to the podium to announce the results.
items.trans: 執行長走上講台宣布結果。

items.usage: 英式拼 sombre。somber mood / tone / colors。反義 cheerful、upbeat。
items.example: The meeting ended on a somber note after the layoff news.
items.trans: 裁員消息傳出後，會議在沉重的氣氛中結束。

items.usage: ultimate goal / outcome / responsibility；副詞 ultimately＝最終。口語 the ultimate…＝最棒的。
items.example: Our ultimate goal is to make the product profitable.
items.trans: 我們的最終目標是讓產品獲利。

items.usage: 形容詞 introspective。比 self-reflection 正式。do some introspection。
items.example: The holiday gave me time for some much-needed introspection.
items.trans: 假期讓我有時間做些早該做的自我反省。

items.usage: 文中較少見的用法：當動詞，強調用心構思：craft a message / a strategy / a statement。名詞 craft＝工藝。
items.example: She carefully crafted her response to the client.
items.trans: 她用心寫了給客戶的回覆。

items.usage: 文中指計畫內容「詳細紮實」；常形容文字難讀：a dense report。原意「稠密的」（dense fog / population）。
items.example: The contract is dense, so read it slowly.
items.trans: 這份合約內容很密，要慢慢讀。

items.term: Imagine that it's (time) in the future, and…
items.usage: 用時間跳躍製造情境，引導讀者從未來回看現在；呼應 #41 Imagine you're… 開場法。
items.example: Imagine that it's five years in the future, and your startup has just gone public.
items.trans: 想像現在是五年後，而你的新創公司剛剛上市。

items.term: Sure, this is…, but it's also…
items.usage: 先讓步承認缺點，再翻轉出價值，語氣自然口語。類似 #42 While X…, it's far more…
items.example: Sure, this is extra work, but it's also a great chance to learn.
items.trans: 當然這是額外工作，但也是很好的學習機會。

items.term: Whenever you…, whether big or small, …
items.usage: whether A or B 插入句中補充「不論哪種情況」。可換成 whether online or offline / whether you like it or not。
items.example: Whenever you make a decision, whether big or small, consider who it affects.
items.trans: 每當你做決定，不論大小，都要想想會影響到誰。

items.usage: After all 提出理由支持前句；without… 引出假設情境。
items.example: Test it carefully. After all, without proper testing, users will find the bugs for us.
items.trans: 要仔細測試。畢竟沒有好好測試，使用者就會幫我們找到錯誤。

items.term: The real benefits of X come when…
items.meaning: X 真正的好處在於……的時候才出現
items.usage: 先肯定一般好處，再強調「真正」價值在哪裡。常以 However 開頭承接前文。
items.example: The real benefits of exercise come when you do it consistently.
items.trans: 運動真正的好處要持之以恆才會出現。

items.usage: jam＝卡住：a paper jam（卡紙）、traffic jam（塞車）、The door is jammed.。口語省略 is → 's。
items.example: Sorry I'm late — the printer jammed again.
items.trans: 抱歉遲到了，印表機又卡紙。

items.usage: on 和 at 都可，on 較常見。比喻：Opportunity is knocking at your door.（機會來敲門）。
items.example: Someone's knocking on the door — can you get it?
items.trans: 有人在敲門，你可以去開嗎？

items.meaning: 要事第一、先做最重要的事
items.usage: 本書第三個習慣。近義 first things first（口語：先處理要緊的）。
items.example: First things first: let's confirm the budget before we plan the event.
items.trans: 先做要緊的事：規劃活動前先確認預算。

items.usage: 插入語，用來換個方式解釋：Put differently, …；近義 in other words、to put it another way。文中 Or put differently: which is… 較口語。
items.example: Sales are flat. Put differently, we're not growing.
items.trans: 業績持平，換句話說，我們沒有成長。

items.usage: 與 #91 ahead of time 同義；in advance of + 事件＝在……之前。thanks in advance＝先謝了（信件結尾）。
items.example: Please book the meeting room in advance.
items.trans: 請提前預約會議室。

items.usage: two-by-two 當形容詞用連字號。顧問、簡報常見 a 2x2 matrix。grid＝格子；power grid＝電網。
items.example: Let's map our options on a two-by-two grid.
items.trans: 我們把選項畫在一個 2×2 的方格上。

items.usage: divide up the work / tasks / money among sb；up 帶「分完」的意味。近義 split up。
items.example: Let's divide up the tasks so everyone knows what to do.
items.trans: 我們分配一下工作，讓大家知道要做什麼。

items.usage: efforts 用複數表示各方面的努力；近義 #54 direct one's energy toward。
items.example: We should focus our efforts on our biggest clients.
items.trans: 我們應該集中心力在最大的客戶上。

items.usage: deserve + N：deserve credit / a raise / a break。deserve 後不加介係詞。
items.example: This section of the report deserves special attention.
items.trans: 報告的這個部分值得特別注意。

items.usage: come with benefits / risks / a warranty。文中 come with the biggest payoffs＝帶來最大回報。
items.example: The new role comes with more responsibility.
items.trans: 這個新職位伴隨更多責任。

items.usage: payoff＝努力後的回報；動詞片語 pay off＝有回報（Hard work pays off.）。
items.example: Training new staff takes time, but the payoff is huge.
items.trans: 培訓新人很花時間，但回報很大。

items.usage: address 當動詞＝處理、應對（address a problem / concern / issue）。early on＝在初期。
items.example: If we address these risks early on, we'll avoid delays later.
items.trans: 如果及早處理這些風險，之後就能避免延誤。

items.usage: 同義 stop / keep A from V-ing。prevent 比 stop 正式。
items.example: Regular backups prevent us from losing important data.
items.trans: 定期備份能防止我們遺失重要資料。

items.meaning: 個人親自處理的細節、人情味
items.usage: add a personal touch＝加點個人風格或心意。文中 tasks that don't need your personal touch＝不必親自處理的事。
items.example: A handwritten note adds a personal touch to the gift.
items.trans: 手寫卡片讓禮物多了份心意。

items.usage: 後接名詞或 V-ing：When it comes to cooking, he's an expert. 注意 to 是介係詞。
items.example: When it comes to negotiating, she's the best on our team.
items.trans: 說到談判，她是我們團隊最強的。

items.usage: tackle a problem / task / issue；比 deal with 更有「主動出擊」的語感。原意（運動）擒抱。
items.example: Let's tackle the hardest task first.
items.trans: 我們先處理最困難的任務吧。

items.meaning: 排定優先順序；優先處理
items.usage: prioritize tasks / safety；名詞 priority（top priority）。英式拼 prioritise。
items.example: You need to prioritize your health over work.
items.trans: 你要把健康擺在工作前面。

items.usage: a sense of urgency（急迫感）、as a matter of urgency。形容詞 urgent。
items.example: There's no sense of urgency on this team.
items.trans: 這個團隊沒有急迫感。

items.usage: 複數 matrices /ˈmeɪ.trə.siːz/ 或 matrixes。商業常見 decision matrix、priority matrix。
items.example: We used a decision matrix to compare the vendors.
items.trans: 我們用決策矩陣來比較供應商。

items.usage: quad- 表「四」。the top-right quadrant＝右上象限（簡報分析常見）。
items.example: Our product sits in the high-quality, low-cost quadrant.
items.trans: 我們的產品落在高品質低成本的象限。

items.usage: 動詞 overlook＝忽略、沒注意到；另義「俯瞰」（a room overlooking the sea）。易混淆 oversee（監督）。
items.example: Customer service is often overlooked by startups.
items.trans: 客服常被新創公司忽略。

items.usage: a pressing issue / need / concern。近義 urgent；文中 don't feel as pressing＝感覺沒那麼急。
items.example: We have more pressing matters to discuss.
items.trans: 我們有更急迫的事要討論。

items.usage: delegate tasks to sb；名詞 delegation。名詞 delegate /ˈdel.ə.ɡət/＝代表（尾音不同）。
items.example: Good managers know when to delegate.
items.trans: 好主管知道什麼時候該授權。

items.meaning: 事必躬親地管理、管太細
items.usage: 貶義；名詞 micromanagement、micromanager。
items.example: Nobody likes a boss who micromanages every email.
items.trans: 沒人喜歡連每封信都要管的老闆。

items.usage: play solitaire；也指單顆鑲嵌的寶石戒指。英式稱紙牌遊戲為 patience。
items.example: He spent the afternoon playing solitaire on his laptop.
items.trans: 他整個下午都在筆電上玩接龍。

items.usage: 把 Here to help 移到句首、主詞放後面，製造「登場」效果。類似 Here comes the bus. / Joining us today is…（主持介紹來賓）。
items.example: Joining us today is our new head of marketing, Amy Lin.
items.trans: 今天加入我們的是新任行銷主管 Amy Lin。

items.usage: 對比兩派做法的簡潔句型（比 #71 少一組）。favor + N / V-ing＝偏好、支持。之後常接 But the real secret is…
items.example: Some favor working from home; others say the office is more productive.
items.trans: 有人偏好在家工作，有人則認為辦公室效率更高。

items.usage: Once + 現在完成式表「一旦完成某步驟」，後句說明好處。適合教學、說明流程。
items.example: Once you've set clear goals, it's easier to say no to distractions.
items.trans: 一旦設定清楚的目標，就比較容易拒絕干擾。

items.term: While X is important, it's really Y that…
items.meaning: 雖然 X 重要，但真正……的是 Y
items.usage: While 讓步＋ it's … that 強調句，凸顯重點。結合 #42 的讓步法。
items.example: While price is important, it's really service that keeps customers coming back.
items.trans: 價格雖然重要，但真正讓顧客回流的是服務。

items.usage: 溫和提醒的口語句型，比 You must 柔和。也可說 Just make sure (that)…
items.example: Feel free to borrow my car. Just be sure to fill up the tank.
items.trans: 車儘管借去，只要記得加滿油。

items.usage: 先否定錯誤做法，再給正確方向，簡潔有力，適合給建議。
items.example: Don't just list problems; instead, suggest a solution.
items.trans: 不要只列問題，而是提出解決方案。

items.usage: take home＝贏得帶回（take home the prize / first place）；take-home pay＝實得薪資。
items.example: Our team took home the trophy for best design.
items.trans: 我們團隊拿下最佳設計獎。

items.usage: empty-handed 常搭 leave / return / go home。商務：leave the negotiation empty-handed。
items.example: We didn't want the client to leave empty-handed, so we offered a discount.
items.trans: 我們不想讓客戶空手而回，所以給了折扣。

items.usage: no matter how + adj./adv. + S + V；也有 no matter what / who / where。
items.example: No matter how busy you are, take a break every hour.
items.trans: 不管多忙，每小時都要休息一下。

items.usage: 商務超常用：a mutually beneficial partnership / agreement / relationship。近義 win-win。
items.example: We're looking for a mutually beneficial partnership.
items.trans: 我們在尋求互惠的合作關係。

items.usage: make (good / full) use of＝善用／充分利用；比 use 正式。
items.example: Make full use of the resources the company offers.
items.trans: 要充分利用公司提供的資源。

items.usage: 可當形容詞：a win-win situation / solution；也可當名詞：look for the win-win。另有 lose-lose（兩敗俱傷）。
items.example: Flexible hours are a win-win for staff and the company.
items.trans: 彈性工時對員工和公司是雙贏。

items.usage: turn potential partners into adversaries；類似 turn an idea into a business、turn a crisis into an opportunity。
items.example: She turned a small side project into a successful business.
items.trans: 她把一個小副業變成成功的事業。

items.usage: breed 原義「繁殖」，引申為「孕育（負面事物）」：breed resentment / conflict。諺語 Familiarity breeds contempt.
items.example: Secrecy breeds distrust in any team.
items.trans: 任何團隊中，秘而不宣都會滋生不信任。

items.usage: top-performing employee / fund / product；名詞 top performer。
items.example: Our top-performing stores are all in city centers.
items.trans: 我們表現最好的門市都在市中心。

items.usage: lead（n.）在業務領域＝潛在客戶線索：sales leads、generate leads。另義「線索」（The police have no leads.）。
items.example: The marketing team generated 200 new leads last month.
items.trans: 行銷團隊上個月開發了 200 個新潛在客戶。

items.term: ditch A in favor of B
items.meaning: 拋棄 A 改用 B
items.usage: ditch＝口語「丟掉、放棄」；in favor of＝選擇（B）而捨棄前者。正式可用 abandon A for B。
items.example: Many companies have ditched paper forms in favor of apps.
items.trans: 很多公司已經捨棄紙本表單，改用 App。

items.usage: involved 放名詞後＝參與其中的：the people involved、the risks involved。
items.example: The new schedule works better for everyone involved.
items.trans: 新時程對所有相關的人都比較好。

items.usage: give out＝分發：give out flyers / prizes / samples。另義「耗盡、故障」（My voice gave out.）。
items.example: The company gives out bonuses at the end of each year.
items.trans: 公司每年年底發獎金。

items.usage: A result in B（A 是因）；易混淆 result from（B result from A，表果）。
items.example: The new system resulted in faster delivery times.
items.trans: 新系統讓交貨時間縮短了。

items.usage: Covey 提出的概念，相對於 scarcity mentality（匱乏心態）。abundant（adj.）充足的。
items.example: An abundance mentality makes it easier to share credit.
items.trans: 有富足心態的人比較容易與人分享功勞。

items.usage: commodity＝商品、原物料（commodity prices）；比喻珍貴的東西：Time is a precious commodity.
items.example: These days, attention is a rare commodity.
items.trans: 如今，注意力是稀缺資源。

items.usage: 比喻目標一致；近義 be on the same side / be on the same page（想法一致）。
items.example: Remember, sales and marketing are playing on the same team.
items.trans: 記住，業務和行銷是同一陣線的。

items.usage: 比 win 正式、有氣勢：triumph over adversity（戰勝逆境）；形容詞 triumphant。
items.example: In the end, common sense triumphed.
items.trans: 最終，常識佔了上風。

items.usage: collaborative effort / approach / tools；動詞 collaborate on sth with sb。
items.example: The report was a collaborative effort between three departments.
items.trans: 這份報告是三個部門合作完成的。

items.usage: dominant position / player / culture；動詞 dominate。
items.example: Apple remains the dominant player in the premium phone market.
items.trans: 蘋果仍是高階手機市場的主導者。

items.usage: 一個字或分寫 world view 皆可；近義 outlook、perspective、paradigm（#35）。
items.example: Traveling widely changed my worldview.
items.trans: 到處旅行改變了我的世界觀。

items.usage: 注意拼字：disaster → disastrous（去掉 e）。disastrous consequences / results。
items.example: The product launch was disastrous.
items.trans: 這次產品上市慘不忍睹。

items.usage: 比 opponent 正式、敵意較強；形容詞 adversarial（對立的）。易混淆 adversity（逆境）。
items.example: In negotiations, treat the other side as a partner, not an adversary.
items.trans: 談判時，要把對方當夥伴，而不是敵人。

items.usage: 正式；常與 conflict、tension 並用。反義 harmony。
items.example: Unequal pay caused disharmony within the team.
items.trans: 薪資不平等造成團隊不和。

items.usage: incentivize sb to do sth；名詞 incentive（financial incentives）。英式 incentivise。
items.example: We incentivize staff to suggest improvements.
items.trans: 我們用獎勵鼓勵員工提出改善建議。

items.usage: 結尾唸 /tɑːʒ/。sabotage a project / sb's chances；自毀：self-sabotage。
items.example: He accused a coworker of sabotaging his presentation.
items.trans: 他指控同事破壞他的簡報。

items.meaning: 滿足感、成就感；（訂單）履行
items.usage: 英式 fulfilment。sense of fulfillment（呼應 #2）；電商：order fulfillment（訂單出貨處理）。
items.example: She finds real fulfillment in teaching.
items.trans: 她從教學中得到真正的滿足。

items.usage: 正式，常接 goal / level / status / success；名詞 attainment。比 achieve 更書面。
items.example: Few athletes ever attain that level of skill.
items.trans: 很少運動員能達到那樣的技術水準。

items.usage: 兩者對比時用 one / the other（三者以上用 others / the rest）。文中 One team takes home the trophy; the other goes home empty-handed.
items.example: One candidate has more experience; the other has fresh ideas.
items.trans: 一位候選人經驗較多，另一位則有新想法。

items.usage: 自問自答的短句，製造節奏與張力，常見於文章、簡報。
items.example: We cut meetings by half. The result? A happier, faster team.
items.trans: 我們把會議砍半。結果呢？團隊更開心、效率更快。

items.usage: 說明前述做法帶來的好處；口語常用。近義 This way、By doing so（較正式）。
items.example: Send me the files tonight. That way, I can review them before the meeting.
items.trans: 今晚把檔案寄給我，這樣我就能在開會前看過。

items.term: There's always more + N + to be had.
items.usage: to be had＝可得到的（被動不定詞）：There's money to be had in…（……有錢可賺）。
items.example: There's always more to be learned from your mistakes.
items.trans: 從錯誤中總有更多可學的。

items.usage: pick out sb / sth from a crowd＝從人群中認出；也可指挑選：pick out a gift。
items.example: Can you pick out your sister in this photo?
items.trans: 你能在這張照片裡認出你妹妹嗎？

items.usage: off 表「從……上面取得」：read the numbers off the screen。
items.example: He just read his speech off the slides.
items.trans: 他只是照著投影片唸講稿。

items.usage: try out a new tool / recipe / idea；try sth on 則專指試穿。
items.example: We're trying out a new project management app.
items.trans: 我們在試用一款新的專案管理 App。

items.usage: 不再追究或補充：Let's just leave it at that.（就這樣吧）。
items.example: He said he was busy, and I left it at that.
items.trans: 他說他很忙，我就沒再追問。

items.usage: approach（n.）＝方法；也可說 take a new / fresh / hands-on approach。
items.example: If this doesn't work, we'll take a different approach.
items.trans: 如果這樣行不通，我們就換個方法。

items.usage: be at the heart of sth＝是某事的關鍵；近義 at the core of。
items.example: Trust is at the heart of every good partnership.
items.trans: 信任是所有良好合作的核心。

items.usage: hone 原指磨刀，比喻精進：hone your writing / negotiating skills。易混淆 home in on（瞄準）。
items.example: She took a course to hone her presentation skills.
items.trans: 她上課磨練簡報技巧。

items.usage: 常說 That's only half the picture. 反義 the full / whole picture、the big picture（大局）。
items.example: Sales numbers only tell half the picture.
items.trans: 銷售數字只呈現了一半的情況。

items.usage: on a personal / emotional / deeper level；在某個層次上理解或連結。
items.example: I connect with this book on a personal level.
items.trans: 這本書讓我在個人層面上很有共鳴。

items.usage: 原指收聽頻道（tune in to the radio）；引申為「留意、理解」他人情緒或需求。反義 tune out（不理會）。
items.example: Good salespeople tune into what customers really want.
items.trans: 好的業務能察覺顧客真正想要什麼。

items.meaning: 參考框架、看事情的角度
items.usage: 每個人理解世界的背景與經驗基礎；近義 perspective、point of view。
items.example: We come from different cultures, so our frames of reference differ.
items.trans: 我們來自不同文化，看事情的角度也不同。

items.usage: hold off on + N / V-ing＝延後做；近義 put off、postpone。
items.example: Let's hold off on hiring until the budget is approved.
items.trans: 在預算核准前先暫緩招人。

items.usage: centered on / around；近義 focused on。customer-centered＝以顧客為中心。
items.example: The discussion was centered on next year's budget.
items.trans: 討論以明年的預算為主。

items.usage: sincere＝真誠的；常見 sincere apology / thanks。信件結尾 Sincerely。
items.example: Great managers have a sincere interest in their team's growth.
items.trans: 好主管真心關注團隊的成長。

items.usage: 近義 gradually、in the long run。易混淆 overtime（加班）。
items.example: Over time, small savings add up.
items.trans: 隨著時間累積，小額儲蓄會積少成多。

items.usage: blurry vision / photo；動詞、名詞 blur。比喻記憶模糊：a blurry memory。
items.example: The photo came out blurry because my hand shook.
items.trans: 因為手抖，照片拍糊了。

items.usage: squint at sth；因強光或看不清而瞇眼。
items.example: She squinted at the tiny print on the label.
items.trans: 她瞇著眼看標籤上的小字。

items.usage: 重音在第二音節。eye doctor 是口語；ophthalmologist 是眼科醫師。
items.example: I need to see an optometrist about new glasses.
items.trans: 我得去找驗光師配新眼鏡。

items.usage: 比 silly / ridiculous 正式；It's absurd to…。名詞 absurdity。
items.example: It's absurd to expect a reply within five minutes.
items.trans: 期望五分鐘內就回覆實在太荒謬。

items.usage: 名詞 empathy（#39）；也作 empathic。empathetic listening＝同理傾聽（本書第五習慣）。
items.example: She's an empathetic manager who listens before judging.
items.trans: 她是有同理心的主管，會先傾聽再判斷。

items.usage: uncover the truth / a problem / hidden costs；近義 discover、reveal。
items.example: The audit uncovered several billing errors.
items.trans: 稽核發現了幾筆帳單錯誤。

items.usage: 文中指深層的感受；商業常見 customer / market sentiment（市場情緒）。I share your sentiment.＝我有同感。
items.example: Customer sentiment has improved since the update.
items.trans: 更新後顧客的觀感有所改善。

items.usage: 比 understand 正式；多用於否定或強調難以理解：I can't comprehend why…。名詞 comprehension。
items.example: I still can't comprehend how they lost the files.
items.trans: 我還是無法理解他們怎麼會把檔案弄丟。

items.usage: 個人經歷的短故事；anecdotal evidence＝個人經驗而非數據的證據。
items.example: He opened the talk with a funny anecdote.
items.trans: 他用一個有趣的小故事開場。

items.usage: 當動詞尾音 /leɪt/；當形容詞 /ɑːrˈtɪk.jə.lət/＝口齒清晰的（an articulate speaker）。
items.example: She articulated the team's concerns clearly.
items.trans: 她清楚表達了團隊的顧慮。

items.usage: reciprocate with sth；形容詞 reciprocal（互相的）。
items.example: If you show respect, people usually reciprocate.
items.trans: 你表現尊重，別人通常也會回報。

items.term: Now, you know how + N + usually go(es).
items.meaning: 你也知道……通常是怎麼回事
items.usage: 用 how sth goes 描述常見流程，拉近與讀者距離：You know how it goes.（你懂的）。
items.example: You know how these meetings usually go: lots of talk, no decisions.
items.trans: 你也知道這種會議通常是怎樣：講很多，沒決定。

items.term: What if, instead of V-ing, S + 過去式…?
items.usage: What if + 過去式＝假設情境；插入 instead of V-ing 做對比。適合提出反常設想。
items.example: What if, instead of hiring more staff, we automated the process?
items.trans: 要是不多請人，而是把流程自動化呢？

items.usage: 用來深化定義：Leadership means more than simply giving orders.
items.example: Listening means more than simply waiting for your turn to talk.
items.trans: 傾聽不只是等著輪到自己說話而已。

items.term: For X to work, you must…
items.meaning: 要讓 X 奏效，你必須……
items.usage: for + 名詞 + to V 當目的：For the plan to succeed, we need…。適合點出必要條件。
items.example: For remote work to work, you must communicate clearly.
items.trans: 要讓遠距工作成功，你必須清楚溝通。

items.term: It takes time, effort, and practice to…
items.usage: It takes + 名詞 + to V；列三項增強語氣。也可加人：It took me years to…
items.example: It takes time, effort, and practice to build trust with a new team.
items.trans: 和新團隊建立信任需要時間、努力和練習。
